subject: Clarify: SOC 2 Type II coverage — end-of-period moment and backups
messages:
From: John D. Lee <john.lee@acmecloud.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Audits International <audits@ai-audit.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 coverage timing question

Hi Vanessa,

We are preparing documentation for our Q2 security intake and had a couple of quick questions about the SOC 2 Type II report you provided:

1) The report lists the covered period as 2026-01-01 through 2026-04-30. For our auditors, we need to confirm whether the report's "end-of-period" snapshot is a point-in-time capture (e.g., 23:59:59 on 2026-04-30) or whether Redwood treats the last day inclusively/exclusively in UTC/local time.

2) Our compliance team also wants to understand whether backups or replica snapshots taken on 2026-05-01 would be considered supporting evidence for the April period (for incident response continuity), or whether those would require a separate bridge letter.

Can you confirm the exact cutoff moment and whether Redwood can provide a short bridge letter to cover evidence continuity for the first 10 days of May while the next Type II is in progress? If helpful, we can loop in our audit contact.

Thanks,
John
John D. Lee
Head of Security, Acme Cloud

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: John D. Lee <john.lee@acmecloud.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage timing question

Hi John — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then details below:

- Cutoff moment: the SOC 2 Type II reporting period we supplied covers 2026-01-01 through 2026-04-30 inclusive. Our documented point-of-capture for the report assertions is 23:59:59 UTC on 2026-04-30.

- Backups/replicas: Backups or replica snapshots taken on 2026-05-01 are not automatically asserted as part of the Type II period because they fall outside the covered timeframe. That said, we can provide a brief bridge letter that: (a) confirms no material control changes between 2026-05-01 and 2026-05-10 and (b) documents the backup/replica schedule and retention so your auditors can rely on the May 1–10 artifacts for continuity.

Looping in Priyom (Compliance) for the technical evidence details and Marissa (Security) for any ancillary notes we should include in the bridge letter. We'll attach the SOC excerpt and a small CSV with daily snapshot timestamps you can share with auditors.

Action: Priyom — can you attach the backup snapshot manifest and the replica lag CSV? Marissa — please flag any control changes in late April/early May that would affect the statement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, John D. Lee <john.lee@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage timing question

Hi all —

Following up with the specifics for the auditors:

- Snapshot schedule: daily full snapshots of customer-facing production databases are taken at 02:00 UTC each day. Incremental backups occur every 4 hours. The snapshot manifest for Apr 30–May 10 is attached (db-replica-lag-report.csv) and lists the exact timestamps and primary/replica IDs.

- Point-in-time definition: our control assertion for the SOC 2 period references system state as of 23:59:59 UTC on 2026-04-30. That is the technical anchor auditors have used historically.

- Replica/lag: replicas apply changes asynchronously with a typical tail lag < 20s under normal load; the attached CSV includes observed lag for Apr 29–May 02.

- Bridge letter: we can produce a short bridge letter that: 1) reiterates the report's covered period and point-in-time anchor, 2) states that no control changes materially affecting the covered controls occurred from 2026-05-01 through 2026-05-10, and 3) lists which backup artifacts exist and how they map to production (by DB ID and timestamp).

Note: ephemeral caches (Redis caches less than 24h TTL) are not considered persistent evidence and will be excluded from the bridge letter — we can note that in the wording so auditors understand what artifacts were relied on.

I attached the CSV manifest for the snapshot timestamps and replica lag. Vanessa/Marissa — happy to sign the bridge letter once we settle final wording.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sr. Manager, Compliance — Redwood Inference
Attachment: db-replica-lag-report.csv (CSV, 14KB)

From: John D. Lee <john.lee@acmecloud.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Audits International <audits@ai-audit.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage timing question

Hi Priyom / Vanessa —

Thanks, that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from our auditor:

- Can the bridge letter explicitly state the timezone anchor (you mentioned 23:59:59 UTC for April 30)? Please include that precise UTC timestamp.

- For the May 1 backups: would you be able to call out which backup artifacts are considered "restorable production points" (e.g., full snapshot at 2026-05-01T02:00:00Z and incremental chain covering that moment)? Auditors like a clear sentence listing exact file IDs or timestamps they can reference.

- Finally, can you confirm that ephemeral caches and short-lived task queues were not relied on for incident forensics? (Sounds like you already excluded them, but they want the explicit line.)

If you can produce a one-page bridge letter with the three bullets above, we can include that as evidence for continuity. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
John

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: John D. Lee <john.lee@acmecloud.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 coverage timing question

Hi John —

We will produce the one-page bridge letter. To confirm the items you requested so the auditors have a final statement:

1) Timezone anchor: The SOC 2 Type II report's point-in-time anchor is 2026-04-30T23:59:59Z (UTC). That exact timestamp will appear in the bridge letter.

2) Restorable production points (examples): Full snapshot: production-db-2026-05-01T02:00:00Z; incremental chain covering 2026-05-01T02:00:00Z through 2026-05-01T14:00:00Z. We'll include the mapping of file IDs/timestamps taken from the attached CSV so auditors can validate.

3) Exclusions: The bridge letter will explicitly state that ephemeral caches (Redis caches with TTL < 24 hours) and transient task-queue state are not used as source evidence for incident investigations and are therefore excluded.

Next steps: Priyom will produce the draft bridge letter and attach it along with the SOC excerpt (redwood_soc2-typeII-excerpt.pdf) and the snapshot manifest CSV. I will deliver the final signed PDF by end of day Monday.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue — Redwood Inference
